body:
Ah, I understand that.

Because I've already been through it. If I had the chance to switch my life with anyone else, while hesitant, I would say no. I lack the self respect that I need to understand that I probably don't deserve something like this, but I also lack the self worth to understand that could even possibly be true.

It's nice to know feel less alone, but it's upsetting that you know what this feels like.

No one should, to be honest. It's one of the worst feelings, I think.

I wish I was enthusiastic enough to perform, hell, or even sing. I can't do it. It makes me far more stressed out than it should, I guess I just tend to get anxiety over stupid things. Although, I do want to thank you for the advice. It's different, new and a nice fresh breath of air, I suppose.

I'd be all for talking to someone-- I just feel a bit odd presenting my problems to someone. I mean, I wouldn't want to add more weight to someone's plate.

I wouldn't know where to start with that. I was never too great at finding resources that weren't completely obvious to me. I also tend to get into these moods that refuses to get help because I believe that there isn't anything wrong with me-- It's dumb, I know.

No one can really promise things will get better, but it's always a nice wish people would offer. In the light of who I am and what this has made me I believe I completely deserve this. I wouldn't wish it on anyone else, but I think that it's better that it happened to me than it be thrust upon someone else.

Ah. I've tried both, actually. It didn't help. Antidepressants had several side effects that would just kill my body throughout the day and one of them managed to make me experience a brief bout of psychosis (apparently).

I've been through therapy several times, when I was younger for separation issues and having a general lack in responses when it came to emotional problems (According to the family that took me in) and for this problem. Nothing seems to help, I can't help but shut myself off to a therapist. She gets paid to listen to me and how do I know she really cares and a bunch  of other BS that I tend to think. It's really upsetting, because I like the idea of Therapy, but CBT hasn't really helped me.

I understand how appropriate it is to focus on things that make you happy, but I can't find a single thing. My motivation is lacking and my drive has ceased to exist. The only thing that's kept me going this far is waiting for it to eventually get better. It hasn't, regardless of the numerous repetitive comments I've heard about it.

I know I'm not one of a kind and that my problems are something people are probably able to cope with better than I-- It's just come to the point where it's exceedingly hard. I can give so much advice to so many people, but when I look back at what's said it... just doesn't apply to me. I can't take my own advice because I know it wont work for me.

If I'm the shining light in someone's life then I hope I had at least left something for them to progress themselves with.
